If it helps somehow, I tried an approach of mimalloc a while ago: https://github.com/DeeJayLSP/godot/commit/eae97092fdf84bd1a2f17ed2cd2160b7909dde96

However, getting it to work properly was beyond my knowledge. I observed there is a `MI_TSAN` define.

One thing that I did manage to do however, was linking with the system-provided mimalloc for Linux packages using `pkg-config mimalloc --cflags --libs`.

This PR performs even better than mine as it override malloc for thirdparty code so more codes benifit from faster memory operations. Hope this can attract some attention on this :)

I investigated the reason for mono build crash. It's due to the `RTLD_DEEPBIND` flag in `dlopen` in `OS::get_singleton()->open_dynamic_library`, which is called by `load_hostfxr`
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/15ff450680a40391aabbffde0a57ead2cd84db56/drivers/unix/os_unix.cpp#L90-L91
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/15ff450680a40391aabbffde0a57ead2cd84db56/drivers/unix/os_unix.cpp#L895

The `RTLD_DEEPBIND` flag makes the dynamic library prioritize using its own defined allocation symbols instead of mimalloc and causes a crash. After removing the flag in `os_unix.cpp`, I can make the mono version work in Linux.

Note in Android, `RTLD_DEEPBIND` is not set in `dlopen`, so mono version works too.

> It's due to the `RTLD_DEEPBIND` flag in `dlopen` in `OS::get_singleton()->open_dynamic_library`, which is called by `load_hostfxr`

We need `RTLD_DEEPBIND` for GDExtensions - see https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/82973

However, it's possible to tell if `open_dynamic_library()` is being used to load a GDExtension or not, by checking if the 3rd argument (`GDExtensionData *p_data`) is set or is `nullptr`. So, one option is to only use it when loading GDExtensions.
Or we could use the approach like #99427, or include `mimalloc-override.h` in `memory.cpp`. (Not sure about the exact reason, but this method won't cause problems in mono build).

> Or we could use the approach like #99427, or include `mimalloc-override.h` in `memory.cpp`. (Not sure about the exact reason, but this method won't cause problems in mono build).

Including `mimalloc-override.h` in memory.cpp creates a broken build, as some code in thirdparty wouldn't be using mimalloc. I tested it once with the TPS demo, and while no crashes happened, some lights had stopped working.

Moreover, [this way doesn't go along well with ThreadSanitizer](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/actions/runs/11989485144/job/33425929157?pr=99427).
I haven't tested it yet. I'm wondering that since this PR breaks Mono, will it also break GDExtension?

> I haven't tested it yet. I'm wondering that since this PR breaks Mono, will it also break GDExtension?

It's worth testing, but it _shouldn't_ break it.

GDExtension already has a mechanism to call into Godot and use Godot's allocator for Godot objects. And if the GDExtension needs to use its own allocator for its own objects, it should continue to do so because of the `RTLD_DEEPBIND`, at least on Linux.

> However, it's possible to tell if `open_dynamic_library()` is being used to load a GDExtension or not, by checking if the 3rd argument (`GDExtensionData *p_data`) is set or is `nullptr`. So, one option is to only use it when loading GDExtensions.

It seems that mimalloc has released several [releases](https://github.com/microsoft/mimalloc?tab=readme-ov-file#releases) this year, and the changelogs mention some bug fixes for macOS. I'm not sure if those would help with our integration. I tried updating the version, but the Windows GCC build failed, which seems related to our custom hack.

Also, should we consider temporarily disabling mimalloc on macOS to help move this PR forward? Since it has been tested on Windows and Linux with real projects.

Is there a plan to advance this PR during the 4.6 development cycle? Since the memory allocator has a relatively wide impact, I think it would be better to get it merged before dev1, so that there will be sufficient time for testing.

This PR won't make it into 4.6 Dev 1. I'm not sure if @RandomShaper plans to maintain it further, but before it could be merged, it would have to be discussed and tested thoroughly. Exchanging the main allocator is a big risk.

If you want to push for progress on this work, we need a build that works on latest `master` that we can test again (the latest build failed unit tests). We would also need extensive performance tests with several real world projects showcasing a consistent improvement. That would at least prove feasibility and motivate reviews.
Finally, I would be interested in arguments being made for any specific allocator (not just choosing `mimalloc` at random). I've noted this [on the proposal](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/11190#issuecomment-2604501965), but `jemalloc` is another contender that also receives high appraisal.

If @RandomShaper does not intend to continue maintaining this branch, I would like to request permission to take it over.

> If you want to push for progress on this work, we need a build that works on latest `master` that we can test again (the latest build failed unit tests).

If you are refering to the CI result in this page, the linux one failed because mimalloc and sanitizer hook the memory API at the same time, macOS ones failed for unknown platform issue and my solution is to disable mimalloc on macOS and in sanitizer builds.

> We would also need extensive performance tests with several real world projects showcasing a consistent improvement. That would at least prove feasibility and motivate reviews.

My initial purpose in proposing a new memory allocator was to mitigate some editor performance issues. Many of them have gone stale because the fixes would break existing behavior, be overly complex, or run into third-party library bottlenecks. Replacing the memory allocator is a feasible solution in the foreseeable future. I have previously run editor performance tests, though the results may need updating (since some SceneTree optimizations were merged recently). Still, I expect a significant performance improvement. As for exported projects, the impact depends heavily on their specific content, so I think it should be made an independent build option that users can enable themselves if needed.

> Finally, I would be interested in arguments being made for any specific allocator (not just choosing `mimalloc` at random). I've noted this [on the proposal](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/11190#issuecomment-2604501965), but `jemalloc` is another contender that also receives high appraisal.

The jemalloc repository is currently archived, and I don’t think an unmaintained third-party library meets our requirements for inclusion. By contrast, the maintainers of mimalloc are quite active and willing to help address issues in various downstream projects.

Also at the moment, we don’t have an available PR for jemalloc, so it makes no sense to compare them now. We can only start discussing the pros and cons of the two libraries if someone is willing to integrate jemalloc.

I think mimalloc sources could be added to the program or library definition in `#platform/<platform>/SCsub`

Based on the fact `#platform` is usually the first directory to compile, and the fact a `builtin_mimalloc` variable with the following `detect.py` block works just fine for `linuxbsd` (assuming, of course, your system has mimalloc development libraries installed):
```py
    if not env["builtin_mimalloc"]:
        env.ParseConfig("pkg-config mimalloc --cflags --libs")
```

I tried this approach in [a branch](https://github.com/DeeJayLSP/godot/tree/mimgd-platform) for macOS and Linux only, and the results were more or less the same. Including the errors, unfortunately.

I managed to get a macOS unit test that doesn't crash at start, but still SIGSEGVs at one test: https://github.com/DeeJayLSP/godot/actions/runs/18046970726/job/51360131908

It seems you need to define `MI_OSX_INTERPOSE` and `MI_OSX_ZONE`.

Just a heads up. We do not intend to merge this anytime soon. We have discussed this at Core meetings a few times and every time we come to the conclusion that we need to re-evaluate the performance impact _after_ we have improved our memory allocation usage patterns. Currently we allocate way more memory at run time than we should. Both in terms of frequency of allocations and size of allocations. 

We are working towards having near zero allocations per frame. In which case the potential performance benefit of mimalloc would be reduced significantly. If we achieve zero allocations per frame, then the benefit of mimalloc would be restricted to load times and may not have much impact.

> We are working towards having near zero allocations per frame.

As an example, I decided to repeat the Dictionary stress test from the [Dictionary reserve PR](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/110709#issue-3436141378). The test itself should have reduced allocations with that PR applied.

Before and after #110709:
```
# Before
time untyped: 7083ms
time typed: 7257ms

# After
time untyped: 6227ms
time typed: 6552ms
```

Before and after #110709 but with `mimalloc` on `LD_PRELOAD`:
```
# Before
time untyped: 4858ms
time typed: 5390ms

# After
time untyped: 4420ms
time typed: 4810ms
```

Therefore:

- Old vs new: 12.25% faster
- Old vs new with mimalloc: 10.98% faster
- Old vs old with mimalloc: 39.92% faster (this is what this PR alone would do)
- New vs new with mimalloc: 38.45% faster

I still think there is a considerable improvement. Maybe it could be a workaround before that work?

Given the current plans to work on reducing allocations first (which makes full sense to me) and therefore it's not prioritary for me to keep trying to polish this PR, I'm marking it as draft. Anyone that wants to take it to the next level, either for own use, experiments or for the potential future reassessment can feel free to take over.
